text:
Maya P.: quick proposal — we need a compact span name + a small set of stable semantic attrs for LLM requests that work across hosted/dedicated/private. goal: easy grouping in the console, cheap exports, and privacy-friendly defaults.

Arjun S.: love it. can you sketch an example?

Maya P.: sketch below. idea: single canonical span name and then attribute bag for details. span name = `rw.infra.llm.request` (signals it's an infra-level request span). attributes (suggested keys):
```
redwood.llm.model.id = "rw-llama-70b"          # canonical model id (no path or tokens)
redwood.llm.model.variant = "q4_0_kv"         # quant/variant tag
redwood.llm.stage = "generate"                # generate|embed|rerank|healthcheck
redwood.llm.input_tokens = 138                  # integer
redwood.llm.output_tokens = 42                  # integer
redwood.llm.batch_size = 4                      # batch size for request
redwood.llm.kvcache_hit = false                 # boolean
redwood.llm.routing = "hosted:us-west-2"      # routing shorthand (tier:region)
redwood.llm.prompt_hash = "sha256:..."         # hash, NOT raw prompt text
redwood.llm.truncation = "truncated_front"     # or none
redwood.request.cost_usd = 0.0021               # derived cost estimate (optional)
```
These give enough for dashboards, SLOs, and cost breakdowns without shipping PII.

Liz K.: curious about the `prompt_hash` — who can reverse it? we should document purpose.

Maya P.: good call. plan: hash + per-customer salt stored in our control plane. internal tooling can map hash->prompt for evals when customer opts in; external exporters get only the hash. privacy default = no raw prompt in traces.

Sophie (eng-observability): also: recommend we mark spans with a sampling hint attr so exporter pipeline can apply rules. e.g. `redwood.telemetry.sampling_hint = "tail:high_error"` or `"keep:1pct"`. helps downstream exporters implement budgeted retention.

Mateo: what about span naming for multi-stage requests? e.g. routing -> model load -> tokenization -> decode. one span or many?

Maya P.: minimal surface: one root `rw.infra.llm.request` with child spans for internal stages when we need them. child span names: `rw.infra.llm.tokenize`, `rw.infra.llm.kv_lookup`, `rw.infra.llm.decode`. keep root attributes for model-level keys. console will group by root span.

Arjun S.: exporter behavior: internal OTLP collector gets full attrs. for third-party or long-term storage we should redact or downsample. propose pipeline:
- collector: receive full trace
- apply policy: if `customer.is_enterprise=true` keep more data
- tail-sampler: keep all error traces + up to 10k errorless traces/day per model
- redact: remove `redwood.prompt_hash` only if flagged by customer
- export: to APM/backends with attr whitelist (model, tokens, kvcache_hit, routing)

Liz K.: retention numbers? we need to set defaults that balance debugging vs cost.

Sophie (eng-observability): propose defaults:
- full trace retention (raw spans) = 14 days for hosted tier free/dev
- full trace retention = 30 days for paid/enterprise
- aggregated daily summaries (counts, p50/p95 latencies, token histograms) = 365 days
- keep histograms + model-level aggregates for 2 years for capacity planning
These are separate from exported copies (we can drop detail when exporting to external sinks).

Mateo: sampling policy specifics?

Sophie (eng-observability): tail-based sampling: always keep all traces with error or latency > 95th. then reservoir sample 0.5% of normal traces per model per region. allow customer override. also keep all traces that hit fallback routing (e.g., downgraded to smaller model).

Arjun S.: console UX request: let teams toggle `redwood.llm.*` attr visibility on dashboards. by default hide prompt_hash/cost_usd but surface model, tokens, kvcache_hit, routing.

Maya P.: also we should standardize naming patterns for tag values to ease grouping: e.g. routing uses `tier:region` (hosted:us-west-2, dedicated:eu-central-1, private:customer-x). model.variant should be short (q8_0, q4_0, fp16).

Mateo: one more: kv cache attribute — we call it `kv_cache_hit` but downstream queries will want hit_rate over time. recommend we emit both `redwood.llm.kvcache_hit` (bool) and `redwood.llm.kvcache_lookup_count` (int) when relevant.

Liz K.: noted. question: what about token attribution for multi-route requests (e.g., reranker calls embedding then gen)?

Maya P.: each root span will include aggregated token counts for the entire logical operation. child spans can include granular token metrics per sub-call. that way dashboards can show both.

Sophie (eng-observability): ops note: we must avoid high-cardinality keys — don't put full model revision SHA in attrs. canonical model id should be stable and short. avoid user ids or email in span attrs by policy.

otel-bot: reminder: OTLP attribute limits -> 32k per span payload. try to keep attr count < 60 to be safe.

Arjun S.: next steps?

Maya P.: I'll draft an RFC with the canonical keys above, retention/sampling defaults, and exporter whitelist rules. please add comments in the RFC PR when I post it. goal to land defaults for hosted + dedicated in two weeks. :sparkles:

Liz K.: thanks — will add a section on compliance (GDPR/CCPA) export controls.

Mateo: +1, will prototype collector filter rules for `redwood.telemetry.sampling_hint`.

Sophie (eng-observability): tagging for dashboards: once RFC lands I'll update dashboard macros to group by `redwood.llm.model.id` and `redwood.llm.routing`.

Maya P.: awesome. that's the plan. ping me with any blockers. :thumbsup:
